Definition: from G1909 and G530; upon one occasion (only):--(at) once (for all).
BiblicalUsage: Ephapax means once, once for all — and it carries the weight of the gospel. Christ died unto sin once; He was seen by above five hundred brethren at once; He offered Himself once, entered the holy place once, and by one offering we are sanctified.
TheologicalSignificance: Once for all is the sweetest phrase in the Bible, and I rest on it. The work is done, it does not need doing again, and I believe a finished sacrifice is the only ground for a settled conscience.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
